strengths: Addresses genuine research gap: Multi-reference text-to-image generation is underexplored; paper convincingly motivates need for comprehensive benchmark.
Rigorous benchmark construction: Careful combination of real and synthetic data, multi-stage filtering (YOLO, SAM, CLIP), manual verification, and category balancing demonstrates meticulous curation.
Comprehensive evaluation framework: Five-criterion evaluation using automated VLMs (Gemini-2.5, GPT-5) plus human validation provides nuanced assessment of model capabilities.

Extensive experimental analysis: Evaluates multiple models (closed and open source), analyzes effects of reference count, provides detailed per-task breakdowns and difficult reference combination analysis.
Identifies practical failure modes: Reveals that background modification, cross-domain composition, and multilingual text rendering remain challenging—valuable insights for driving future research.
Well-documented and reproducible: Detailed construction pipeline in appendix, promises code/data release, enables reproducibility and builds community resource.
Practical impact demonstration: Proposed agent frameworks show measurable improvements, proving benchmark can drive methodological innovation.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Proposed agent frameworks (IPR, CAFG, SRA) are straightforward combinations of existing techniques (prompt refinement, feedback generation, reference adaptation) without significant novel insights.

Shallow root-cause analysis: Paper identifies what models struggle with but provides limited investigation into why multi-reference composition is fundamentally challenging—misses opportunity for deeper understanding.
Incomplete experimental comparisons: OmniGen2 and other models cannot process more than 5 references, limiting fair evaluation; some recent methods may not be included; comparison breadth is limited.

Human evaluation scalability concerns: Final validation relies on human judgment despite VLM automation; raises questions about inter-rater reliability, reproducibility, and scalability of the evaluation protocol.

Lacks theoretical contribution: Paper does not articulate fundamental principles distinguishing multi-reference from single-reference generation or develop theoretical understanding of composition challenges.
Dataset generalization uncertainty: Benchmark based on specific categorization scheme; unclear how performance transfers to real-world multi-reference scenarios beyond constructed benchmark domain.

Incomplete reproducibility details: Exact filtering thresholds not fully specified, Gemini annotation protocol lacks detail, inter-annotator agreement not reported, VLM evaluation procedure could be more transparent.

Multilingual evaluation limitations: Chinese and Japanese text rendering evaluated with limited scope; paper acknowledges model capability gaps but doesn't deeply analyze multilingual-specific challenges.
Missing ablation studies: No systematic investigation of design choices (e.g., why specific number of reference images, category selection) or sensitivity analysis.

Scope limitations: Focuses on specific editing/generation scenarios; does not explore other potentially important dimensions (video temporal consistency, very large reference sets, constraint-based editing).

strengths: Addresses genuine gap in multi-reference image generation evaluation; existing benchmarks focus on single-reference scenarios
Comprehensive and systematic task design with four base structures and orthogonal difficulty dimensions (cross-domain, scale/viewpoint, rare concepts, multilingual)
Rigorous data construction with careful filtering (YOLO, SAM, CLIP), manual verification, and effort to balance real vs. synthetic data
Multi-faceted evaluation across five well-chosen dimensions (Instruction Alignment, Reference Consistency, Background-Subject Match, Physical Realism, Visual Quality)
Valuable empirical insights about performance degradation with reference count, challenges in cross-domain settings, and multilingual text rendering failures
Excellent presentation with detailed radar charts, failure case visualizations, and qualitative examples that effectively communicate benchmark scope
weaknesses: Critical flaw in evaluation methodology: frames VLM evaluation (Gemini-2.5, GPT-5) as 'human evaluation' without validation against ground-truth human judgment; lacks inter-annotator agreement metrics and reproducibility is compromised by dependence on proprietary models
No novel methodological contributions—purely a benchmark paper; agentic frameworks (IPR, CAFG, SRA) are straightforward applications of existing techniques, not novel approaches

Insufficient statistical rigor: lacks confidence intervals, significance tests, bootstrap analysis; arbitrary weighting scheme (3,3,1,1,1) for evaluation metrics unexplained; no inter-rater agreement statistics
Limited and inaccessible model coverage: only 5 models evaluated including proprietary systems (GPT-Image-1, Qwen); reproduction and extension by other researchers infeasible

Reproducibility gaps: code unavailable at review; proprietary VLM judges prevent reproduction; task selection process unclear (why exactly 48 tasks?); manual curation steps underdocumented; VLM evaluation consistency unexplored

Shallow analysis of key findings: performance degradation with reference count observed but not mechanistically explained; limited investigation of architectural failures; cross-domain analysis remains qualitative
Missing critical elements: no human evaluator comparison, no computational cost analysis, no assessment of output diversity, unclear real vs. synthetic data split per task

strengths: Addresses a genuine and important gap: systematically identifies and tackles the limitation that existing benchmarks focus on single/few-reference scenarios while practical multi-reference generation is more complex

Comprehensive and carefully constructed benchmark: thoughtfully designed across multiple orthogonal dimensions (reference count 3-8, cross-domain diversity, scale mismatches, rare concepts, multilingual rendering) with 3,769 diverse tasks
Rigorous evaluation framework: five well-motivated metrics evaluated via both automated VLM assessment (Gemini 2.5, GPT-5) and human evaluation with comprehensive per-task and per-metric breakdown

Valuable empirical insights: clearly demonstrates performance degradation with increasing references, systematically identifies failure modes (cross-domain, scale/viewpoint, rare concepts, multilingual text), and provides honest assessment of limitations

Strong reproducibility prospects: promises to release dataset and code, provides detailed construction methodology, clear evaluation protocols, extensive supplementary material with prompts and detailed results
Clear presentation and comprehensive analysis: well-written with informative figures and extensive qualitative examples demonstrating both successes and failures across reference combinations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: contribution is primarily infrastructural/empirical rather than methodological; no novel generation methods, metrics, or architectural advances

Evaluation methodology concerns: heavy reliance on VLM-based automatic evaluation may introduce systematic biases; human evaluation rigor unclear (no inter-rater agreement metrics reported, scale of human evaluation not fully specified, no discussion of annotator disagreement resolution)
Incomplete validation: no reported correlation between MultiBanana scores and performance on existing benchmarks; VLM evaluation quality not independently validated against human judgment
Limited model coverage: only 5 models evaluated with missing contemporary architectures (FLUX, Stable Diffusion 3 not included); limited architectural diversity reduces generalizability of findings

Dataset scope limitations: restricted to text-to-image only (no video/3D); maximum 8 references may not capture full real-world complexity; aesthetic/resolution filtering thresholds may bias dataset; synthetic data usage could introduce circular dependency

Underdeveloped agentic framework section: Section 4.4 feels preliminary and disconnected from main benchmark narrative, testing only three frameworks with modest improvements (~4-6%) and lacking analysis of which failure modes are addressed

Limited experimental analysis: no statistical significance testing reported; no ablation studies on benchmark construction choices (optimal reference count, synthetic vs. real data importance, filtering impact); missing variance analysis across categories

Generalization concerns: evaluation focuses on artistic/photorealistic generation with unclear applicability to other visual styles or domain-specific tasks; scope primarily limited to English and Chinese for multilingual aspects

strengths: Addresses important gap: Systematic benchmark for multi-reference text-to-image generation that existing benchmarks don't adequately cover
Comprehensive benchmark design: 3,769 images with 36 task types covering 5 diversity factors (cross-domain, scale/viewpoint, rare concepts, multilingual text, varying reference counts)

Rigorous multi-faceted evaluation: Five well-motivated metrics with multiple independent VLM judges showing reasonable correlation (0.55-0.65 Spearman), tested on both closed-source and open-source models
Clear quantitative insights: Demonstrates and systematically analyzes performance degradation with increasing references across different task difficulties and model types
Thorough documentation: Detailed appendices with evaluation criteria, prompts, and construction procedures supporting reproducibility
Systematic failure analysis: Categorizes failure modes with qualitative examples (Figure 6) linking performance degradation to specific challenging conditions
weaknesses: Limited effectiveness of proposed solutions: Agentic frameworks (IPR, CAFG, SRA) show only modest improvements with some configurations degrading performance, insufficient analysis of why these approaches fail

Heavy VLM-based evaluation with limited human validation: Only 32 human-evaluated samples insufficient to validate VLM scores comprehensively; relies on proprietary models (GPT-5, Gemini) raising reproducibility concerns

Synthetic data contamination: Incorporates artifacts from Nano Banana and GPT-Image-1 in benchmark construction, creating circularity; subjective quality filtering criteria ('visually appealing') not well-validated

Incomplete technical analysis: Demonstrates model degradation but doesn't provide deep mechanistic understanding of failure causes; limited ablation studies and investigation of reference combination strategies

Moderate model and task coverage: Only 5 models tested; OmniGen2 saturation suggests unequal challenge level; ~105 images per task type with likely undersampling of rare concepts and multilingual tasks

Presentation and scope issues: Figures 15-17 are crowded and difficult to read; multilingual component minimally evaluated despite being listed as key diversity factor; doesn't address scope limitations (static images only, no temporal consistency)

strengths: Addresses important gap in multi-reference image generation evaluation with a large, well-constructed benchmark (3,769 samples, 36 task types)
Comprehensive dataset design covering diverse scenarios: cross-domain diversity, scale/viewpoint mismatches, rare concepts, multilingual text, and multiple editing task types
Thorough evaluation protocol with 5 complementary metrics and detailed per-task analysis across challenging reference combinations
Well-documented benchmark construction pipeline with clear filtering and quality control procedures
Extensive supplementary analysis including VLM judge reliability assessment, agentic framework experiments, and difficult reference combination analysis
Commitment to reproducibility with promised dataset/code release and detailed implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily a benchmark/dataset paper with no novel algorithmic or methodological contributions; metrics are combinations of existing approaches
Moderate VLM evaluation reliability: Pearson correlations with human judgment are 0.58-0.62 (moderate, not strong); insufficient for robust primary evaluation metric
Insufficient human evaluation: only 32 image samples used for human-VLM correlation study with no inter-rater reliability reported among human judges
Synthetic data composition concern: ~45% of dataset uses synthetically generated images to balance categories, potentially introducing systematic biases favoring certain model architectures
Incomplete model coverage: only 5 models evaluated; many contemporary multi-reference generation models are omitted, limiting benchmark comprehensiveness

Vague evaluation criteria and metric definitions: Reference Consistency aggregation across multiple references unclear; metric decomposition lacks theoretical justification or empirical validation; some criteria appear overlapping
Limited actionable insights: benchmark reveals problems but provides minimal guidance on how to improve models; agentic framework experiments show only marginal gains
Statistical rigor gaps: standard deviations rarely reported, no significance testing between model comparisons, informal definition of 'difficult reference combinations'
Presentation issues: 38 pages of dense content; key findings buried in extensive tables; radar charts (Figures 15-17) too small to interpret effectively

Methodological concerns: arbitrary filtering criteria (e.g., CLIP similarity > 20, bounding box thresholds), no justification for Gemini selection for instruction generation, detailed evaluation prompts may introduce subtle biases

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap in existing benchmarks for multi-reference image generation, with systematic evaluation across diverse challenge types (3-8 references, cross-domain, scale mismatches, rare concepts, multilingual text)

Comprehensive and carefully constructed dataset with 3,769 images, rigorous filtering (aesthetic score >6.25, resolution >512), balanced categorization across 6 major and 18 subcategories, and deliberate inclusion of diversity factors
Robust evaluation methodology with five well-motivated criteria validated against human judgments (r=0.6-0.7 correlation), multiple VLM judges, and proper self-consistency analysis

Systematic analysis demonstrating clear patterns of model degradation with multiple references and identification of specific failure modes, with insightful distinction between closed-source (visual coherence) and open-source (instruction following) strengths

Excellent reproducibility documentation including detailed appendices covering image collection, filtering, task construction, VLM evaluation prompts, and specific implementation details with API versions
Rigorous experimental evaluation with per-task and per-category detailed results, analysis of difficult reference combinations, and VLM judge reliability validation with human correlation analysis
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty with the paper primarily contributing a benchmark rather than new algorithms; agentric framework contributions (IPR, CAFG, SRA) are straightforward adaptations showing only modest improvements (Table 5)

Evaluation design concerns including moderate human-VLM correlation (0.6-0.7), small human evaluation subset (32 samples) without detailed subset selection methodology, and missing ablation studies justifying the specific five evaluation criteria

Dataset construction limitations including heavy reliance on synthetic data (Nano Banana, GPT-Image-1) that could introduce training biases, subjective filtering criteria, residual category imbalance in Figure 3, and potential biases from YOLOv12 object detection

Shallow analysis of failure modes with demonstrated failures but limited explanation of underlying causes; while cross-domain and scale mismatches are identified, prescriptive guidance for model improvements is weak

Scope limitations including explicit exclusion of video generation and temporal consistency, text rendering restricted to three languages, maximum 8 references that may not generalize to scenarios with many more references, and approximately 700 image pairs raising generalization concerns

Presentation issues including dense 38-page document with difficult-to-parse radar charts in Figures 15-17, weak connection between identified problems and actionable solutions, and key results (Qwen3-VL) relegated to appendix without full integration into main narrative
